questions.exp: Qutb-ud-din Aibak founded the Delhi Sultanate in 1206 AD after the death of Muhammad Ghori. He established the Slave Dynasty, the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.q: The Qutb Minar was built by which ruler?
questions.exp: The Qutb Minar was started by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and completed by Iltutmish. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Delhi.

questions.q: Who was the first woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.exp: Razia Sultana (1236–1240) was the first and only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. She was the daughter of Iltutmish who appointed her as his successor.

questions.q: The Battle of Panipat (First) was fought between whom?
questions.exp: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi. Babur's victory established the Mughal Empire in India.

questions.q: Akbar's famous policy of religious tolerance was called?
questions.exp: Din-i-Ilahi (Divine Faith) was Akbar's syncretic religion founded in 1582. It combined elements of Islam, Hinduism, Zoroastrianism, and Christianity.
The Taj Mahal was built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. It was completed in 1653 and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.q: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in which year?
questions.exp: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I. It was one of the greatest Hindu empires of medieval India.

opts: A Afghan king who defeated Humayun
questions.exp: Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun in 1540 and established the Sur Empire. He introduced significant administrative reforms including the Grand Trunk Road.

questions.q: The Bhakti Movement in South India was started by?
questions.exp: The Bhakti Movement in South India was pioneered by the Alvars (Vaishnava saints) and Nayanmars (Shaiva saints) between the 6th and 9th centuries CE.

questions.q: The last major ruler of the Mughal Empire was?
questions.exp: Bahadur Shah Zafar (1837–1857) was the last Mughal Emperor. He was exiled to Rangoon after the 1857 revolt and died there in 1862.
